builds.name: Reference: Ranked top core
builds.goal: Reference for Dr. Mundo: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ top players use most (3,878 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 62% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A regenerating juggernaut who converts health into attack damage and wins by repeatedly reaching a slowed enemy. Canister recovery and a well-timed W/R sustain window are central. The current top provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Warmog's Armor → Heartsteel → Titanic Hydra. Grasp of the Undying keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Boots of Swiftness, Spirit Visage, Thornmail.
builds.summary: The proven top baseline: Warmog's Armor → Heartsteel → Titanic Hydra, with Grasp of the Undying.
testPlan: Play it in top as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Warmog's Armor → Heartsteel → Titanic Hydra) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 62% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Warmog's Armor → Heartsteel → Titanic Hydra.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

If the enemy is killed, Mundo swats them away, dealing [5 / 15 / 25 / 35 / 45 + (0.05) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]] physical damage to enemies they pass through.

Dr. Mundo pumps himself with chemicals, gaining [(0.15 / 0.2 / 0.25) × 100]% of his missing Health as max Health, [(0.15 / 0.25 / 0.35) × 100]% Move Speed, and regenerating [(0.2 / 0.4 / 0.6) × 100]% max Health over [10] seconds.

At Rank 3, both healing effects are increased by an additional [5]% per nearby enemy champion.

Dr. Mundo hurls his bonesaw, dealing [(0.2 / 0.225 / 0.25 / 0.275 / 0.3) × 100]% current Health magic damage to the first enemy hit and Slowing them by [40]% for [2] seconds.

If the bonesaw hits a champion or monster, Dr. Mundo restores [(1) × (50 / 60 / 70 / 80 / 90)] Health. If it hits a non-champion or non-monster, Dr. Mundo instead restores [(0.5) × (50 / 60 / 70 / 80 / 90)] Health.

builds.name: Medical bag AD conversion
builds.summary: Test medical bag ad conversion against the conventional damage pattern at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test medical bag ad conversion against the conventional damage pattern at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Blunt Force Trauma passively grants 2-3.2% source health as AD; Bloodmail adds a separate bonus-health conversion and Titanic adds attack pressure. Maximum Dosage increases max health and regeneration, making timed E attacks the payoff rather than pretending bonesaws scale with AD.
testPlan: Required state: Earn realistic Heartsteel stacks and use R before the finishing E trade.
Record E attack damage before and during R at equal missing-health percentages.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Healing reduction and percent-health damage punish the huge health pool.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Health conversions are additive hypotheses, not recursive infinite AD.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Heartsteel, Overlord's Bloodmail, Titanic Hydra, Spirit Visage, Sterak's Gage, Plated Steelcaps. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Magic matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Dr. Mundo: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A regenerating juggernaut who converts health into attack damage and wins by repeatedly reaching a slowed enemy. Canister recovery and a well-timed W/R sustain window are central. Measure the health-to-AD conversion, canister recovery and W/R healing window. AP is not assumed to improve this health-driven attack route; count actual target contact. MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure.
builds.summary: MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure.
testPlan: Kit question for Dr. Mundo: Measure the health-to-AD conversion, canister recovery and W/R healing window. AP is not assumed to improve this health-driven attack route; count actual target contact.

Start with the early core (Hollow Radiance or other MR first when justified) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: None. Do not treat mana regeneration as None recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Dr. Mundo throws an infected bonesaw, dealing damage to the first enemy hit based on their current health and slowing them. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: MR is wasted against the wrong threat; nearby aura range and healing eligibility matter.

The route fails Dr. Mundo's stated kit question: Measure the health-to-AD conversion, canister recovery and W/R healing window. AP is not assumed to improve this health-driven attack route; count actual target contact.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: MR is wasted against the wrong threat; nearby aura range and healing eligibility matter.
Full cost 15,600 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Hollow Radiance or other MR first when justified. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Abyssal Mask, Spirit Visage, Jak'Sho, The Protean are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: None. Do not treat mana regeneration as None recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Bonesaw resistance execution
builds.summary: Test bonesaw resistance execution against the conventional damage pattern at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test bonesaw resistance execution against the conventional damage pattern at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Infected Bonesaw removes 20-30% current health as magic damage without an AP ratio; Blade supplies an independent physical current-health attack. Trinity follows cleaver casts with physical Spellblade while resistances let Mundo remain for W's gray-health detonation.
testPlan: Required state: Land Q first and detonate W on a champion after absorbing damage.
Compare Q then three attacks against different health and resistance targets.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Bonesaw weakens as health drops and lack of mobility loses attacks.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: AP purchases do not improve the documented bonesaw percentage; W needs a champion hit for full gray healing.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
